rv.q: The show is an altogether more pleasurable experience than that doubly dubious distinction might make it sound.
It's much better than that suggests – enjoyable and more than a little camp.
My own reaction, having seen the finished product, is more one of mild dismay.
A jukebox musical, yes, but it packs an almighty punch.
Headley is superb and diehard fans of the film won't be disappointed; the performance I saw ended with dancing in the aisles.
Watching 'The Bodyguard' is like watching a slick Hollywood blockbuster unfold live in front of you, and that's no bad thing.

cn.t: Critics find this stage adaptation of the 1992 film technically proficient but dramatically hollow, elevated primarily by Heather Headley's mesmerizing vocals delivering Whitney Houston's beloved hits in what amounts to a polished jukebox musical.
